commands.command: node .tmp/detect-case-drift.mjs (git ls-files vs real on-disk names)
commands.details: CI CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT THAT NO LOCAL CHECK COULD SEE. 5 files had been renamed in place with a case-only change (AppModalActions/AppModalActions -> appModalActions, RailSummary -> railSummary, TableAction -> tableAction, TableColumnPriority -> tableColumnPriority, TableColumnWidth -> tableColumnWidth). Windows and macOS filesystems are case-insensitive, so git never noticed the rename: the index kept the OLD casing while the working tree had the new one. Every local check therefore passed (tsc, eslint, vite build, vitest 163/163) because the case-insensitive resolver found the file either way. On Linux CI the import specifiers no longer matched the tracked filenames, so Frontend Contract (check:import-path-case: 13 problems), Frontend Unit Tests (5 suites: 'Failed to resolve import "./patterns/table/tableAction"') and Quality Gates all failed. This is precisely the class of defect the review's correspondence axis was meant to surface, and it is the strongest argument for keeping these gates blocking.

Recorded the 5 case-only renames as explicit two-step moves, because a single-step `git mv Old.ts new.ts` is a no-op on a case-insensitive filesystem. Re-verified: detect-case-drift reports 'tracked files: 2199, not on disk: 0, case mismatch: 0', and check:import-path-case reports 'import path case guard passed for 248 source files'.

commands.details: Mechanical proof that the runtime contract is untouched, rather than an assertion. The 20 componentKey registry keys are byte-identical between main and HEAD — only the import() target paths changed. Same comparison for the permission-code literals under backend/modules/system (116 distinct values, identical) and for the API route path literals across backend/ and frontend/ (60 distinct values, identical). This is the evidence for the runtimeGap claim below.

runtimeGap: None. The remediation is structural only: no API route, database row, permission code, menu componentKey or runtime behaviour changed. Verified mechanically, not asserted — the 20 componentKey registry keys, the 116 permission-code literals under backend/modules/system and the 60 API route path literals across backend/ and frontend/ are all byte-identical between main and HEAD; only physical paths and import specifiers moved. check:menu-contract (16 menus / 20 routes / 89 permissions / 20 component keys) passes as part of the pre-build gate chain.
knownGaps: Case-only renames are invisible on case-insensitive filesystems, and this bit twice. First: 5 in-place case-only renames (the 5 PascalCase .ts -> camelCase .ts fixes) were not recorded by git — the index kept the old casing while the working tree had the new one, so every local check passed on Windows while Linux CI failed. Second: frontend/scripts/check-shell-visual-contract.mjs hardcodes the filename 'AppModalActions.ts' as a path segment, which also only fails on a case-sensitive filesystem. Both are fixed. Sensor coverage is adequate — check:import-path-case caught the import half, and the hardcoded-path half fails loudly (ENOENT / UNRESOLVED_IMPORT) on Linux CI. A local-detectable gate was investigated and REJECTED: the narrow rule 'any hardcoded source-file basename in frontend/scripts must exist under src/ with exact case' yields 34 findings on the current tree, essentially all false positives (package.json, .spec.ts, index.js, List.tsx templates, dashboard.css inside a docstring), so shipping it would require a large allowlist — which is the opposite of fixing a root cause. The actionable rule for developers is therefore: perform case-only renames as a two-step `git mv`, and confirm with a git-index-vs-disk name comparison (note that fs.existsSync is useless for this on Windows/macOS, since it is case-insensitive too).

This machine cannot spawn child processes from Node (spawnSync git/node fails with EBUSY), so the three gates that shell out to git — check:structure, check:harness-encoding, and the tests/scripts suites — cannot run locally. check:structure was therefore verified with the same script reading an injected `git ls-files` file list (identical rule code, only the enumeration replaced); check:harness-encoding is unchanged by this task and is CI-only. The two tests/scripts suites run in CI via `npm run test:scripts` (ci.yml) and were verified locally by driving the gate directly against the same fixtures.

SonarCloud's new-code duplication gate fails (3.54% vs a 3% threshold) and this is an artefact of the move, not of new duplication. The PR adds 1565 lines but SonarCloud reports new_lines = 21030, because files whose content changed while moving (the frontend files, whose import specifiers had to be rewritten) are not recognised as moves and are counted as new code. The pre-existing duplication inside those moved files then counts as new duplication — 744 duplicated lines, dominated by backend/modules/system/i18n/i18n_service_test.go (187), frontend/src/modules/system/audit/OperationLogList.tsx (152), frontend/src/modules/system/iam/role/RoleList.tsx (130), permission_service_test.go (124) and dept_service_test.go (116), none of which this change authored. The repository's own Duplication Gate passes. SonarCloud is NOT one of the ruleset's required checks (the required set is Quality Gates, Security Gates, Unit Tests, CI Summary), so this does not block the merge; it is recorded here so the number is not mistaken for newly introduced duplication. Fixing it would mean refactoring pre-existing duplication in files this change only relocated, which is outside the scope and would obscure the diff.
